title: Private VPC: Topology Editor & Cluster Status Hub (console UX prototype)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Design a focused console surface for Private/VPC customers that combines an interactive network topology editor with a lightweight cluster status hub. This surface should make it fast for platform engineers to: visualize cluster layout, inspect private networking (subnets, peering, NAT/GW), surface upgrade/rollout state, and see cost/latency signals for each cluster.

Scope: Topology canvas (drag-to-arrange nodes), cluster card list with health and current release, status timeline for recent events, quick upgrade controls (canary/rollout/fallback), and a compact cost & latency breakdown per cluster. Include contextual help for RBAC and KMS requirements. Prototype must be responsive to console widths and support keyboard nav for accessibility.

Constraints & assumptions: Work within existing console theming and components; reuse cluster-card, toast/notification, and rollout modal components where possible. Backend endpoints for topology persistence provided by ENG-2456; rollout API surface depends on ENG-2499. Avoid introducing new backend fields unless essential. Prototype should not assume cross-account topology edits — initial iteration is single-tenant only.

Key screens/components:
- Topology Canvas: canvas grid, add/remove nodes, link creation (peerings, route tables), node details panel (metrics snapshot, IP ranges, security groups).
- Cluster Status Hub: sortable list of clusters with inline health microcharts, latest event badge, upgrade status pill, and cost-per-hour estimate.
- Upgrade/Rollout Panel: canary slider, target subset selector, preflight checklist, rollback button.
- Cost & Performance Insights: small sparkline for token-ms latency, estimated monthly cost, suggestions (e.g., "enable KV cache" or "lower batching for low-latency routes").
- Incident banner & timeline: full-width banner for active incidents and a per-cluster timeline of recent health events.
- Onboarding flow: short modal to guide first-time users through topology basics and security reminders.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype with topology canvas, cluster hub, and rollout modal flows
Design annotations for all interactive states and keyboard accessibility notes
Hand-off spec for frontend with component mapping and copy for tooltips/help text
Usability session results (n=5 platform engineers) with no critical usability blockers
Design reviewed and signed off by Product (Oliver Hayes) and Security (Nadia Patel)
updates: 2026-03-01 - Ticket created; initial brief approved by PM (Oliver Hayes).
2026-03-03 - Kickoff workshop with Eng (lead: Diego Mora) to align on API constraints (ENG-2456). Noted backend will return 'peeringType' and 'routeState' fields.
2026-03-05 - First wireframes complete: focused on canvas-first UX rather than list-first after stakeholder feedback. Shared in design critique.

2026-03-07 - Usability quicktest (3 internal platform engineers): topology drag felt natural; discoverability of upgrade controls was low. Action: add persistent "Upgrade" affordance on cluster cards.

2026-03-09 - Design critique with PM and Security: Security requested an inline KMS/role badge on cluster cards and a stronger warning for upgrade actions that touch network-critical nodes. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10 - Prototype iteration: added cost sparkline, incident banner behavior, and keyboard focus states. Prepared handoff notes for frontend.
2026-03-11 - Design review meeting: Eng signaled dependency ENG-2499 for rollout API. Minor UI change requested: move 'rollback' to secondary action inside rollout modal with confirmation.

2026-03-12 - Submitted Figma prototype and annotated spec for In Review. Requested security sign-off and schedule dev grooming with Eng owners. Next: usability test with external beta customer and adjust copy based on legal review.
notes_for_engineering: Persist topology as adjacency list via existing topology endpoint (ENG-2456), avoid frequent full-canvas saves; use optimistic local saves with background sync.
Rollout interactions assume canary API returns progress percent and allow 'pause' and 'rollback' commands (ENG-2499). Implement idempotent actions.
Cost estimates are client-calculated from token-rate and GPU-hour rates; backend will supply current price-per-GPU (placeholder until pricing API available).
Accessibility: canvas must support keyboard pan/zoom and node selection; ensure ARIA labels for nodes and links.
